message.content:
Here’s a quick snapshot of some of the most celebrated composers who have made their mark in the United States—spanning classical, jazz, film, and popular music:

| Composer | Era / Genre | Notable Works / Contributions |
|----------|-------------|--------------------------------|
| **John Philip Sousa** (1854‑1932) | Classical/Patriotic marches | “The Stars and Stripes Forever,” “Washington Post” |
| **Scott Joplin** (1868‑1917) | Ragtime | “Maple Leaf Rag,” “The Entertainer” |
| **George Gershwin** (1898‑1937) | Jazz/Classical crossover | “Rhapsody in Blue,” “An American in Paris,” “Porgy & Bess” |
| **Aaron Copland** (1900‑1990) | Classical | “Appalachian Spring,” “Fanfare for the Common Man,” “Rodeo” |
| **Leonard Bernstein** (1918‑1990) | Classical/Film | “West Side Story,” “Candide,” “On the Town” |
| **Philip Glass** (born 1937) | Minimalism | “Einstein on the Beach,” “Glassworks,” “Koyaanisqatsi” |
| **John Williams** (born 1942) | Film | “Star Wars,” “Indiana Jones,” “Jurassic Park” |
| **Samuel Barber** (1910‑1981) | Classical | “Adagio for Strings,” “Knoxville: Summer of 1915” |
| **William Grant Still** (1895‑1978) | Classical (African‑American composer) | “Afro-American Symphony,” “Bluebird of Happiness” |
| **Charles Ives** (1874‑1954) | Experimental/Modernist | “The Unanswered Question,” “Central Park in the Dark” |
| **George Gershwin** (1898‑1937) | Jazz/Classical crossover | “Rhapsody in Blue,” “An American in Paris,” “Porgy & Bess” |
| **John Adams** (born 1947) | Contemporary classical | “Nixon in China,” “Short Ride in a Fast Machine” |
| **Steve Reich** (born 1936) | Minimalism | “Music for 18 Musicians,” “Different Trains” |
| **Bobby McFerrin** (born 1950) | Vocal jazz | “Don't Worry, Be Happy,” “The Art of the Song” |
| **Kurt Weill** (1900‑1950) | Musical theatre | “The Threepenny Opera,” “Mahagonny” |
| **Duke Ellington** (1899‑1974) | Jazz | “Mood Indigo,” “Take the A Train” |
| **Miles Davis** (1926‑1991) | Jazz | “Kind of Blue,” “Bitches Brew” |
| **Herbie Hancock** (born 1940) | Jazz/Funk | “Head Hunters,” “Cantaloupe Island” |
| **Bob Dylan** (born 1941) | Folk/Rock | “Blowin’ in the Wind,” “Like a Rolling Stone” |
| **Leonard Bernstein** (1918‑1990) | Classical/Film | “West Side Story,” “Candide,” “On the Town” |

### How to Use This List
- **Research**: Dive deeper into each composer’s biography and catalog to understand their influence on American music.
- **Listening**: Start with the highlighted works; they’re often considered entry points into each composer’s oeuvre.
- **Education**: If you’re teaching or learning about American music history, this table can serve as a quick reference or a starting point for deeper exploration.

Feel free to let me know if you’d like more details on any particular composer or if you’re interested in a specific genre or time period!
